## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Python-bytecode stack machine. Executes the opcode
set in py_core_pkg directly: 33-bit small-int arithmetic, compares,
locals, globals, jumps, function calls, native mem32 load/store over an
AXI4-Lite master, and one level of interrupts. Anything outside the fast path
(heap objects, bigints, unknown opcodes) raises a trap and the core
stalls with trap_pc_o at the faulting instruction, so a helper
(microcode or a small RISC-V) can emulate it and resume at
resume_pc_i.

Calls - CALL pushes the return address on a return stack and gives the
callee a fresh frame of N_LOCALS locals (frame 0 is the main program).
Arguments travel on the operand stack: the callee's first instructions
pop them into its locals. RETURN pops the frame and leaves the return
value on the operand stack. N_FRAMES bounds the call depth (deeper is
TRAP_STACK, i.e. RecursionError). Locals are not cleared on entry; the
compiler only reads locals it has assigned.

Interrupts - irq_i is a level input, sampled between instructions when
IRQ_ENABLE has run, no handler is active and a frame is free. Entry is
a call to the SET_IRQ_VECTOR address that also saves the operand stack
depth; RETURN_FROM_IRQ returns and restores it. Handlers may call
functions. Globals are shared, which is how handlers pass data to the
main program. No nesting: irq_i is ignored while a handler runs.

WAIT_IRQ (v2) stops the core until irq_i is high, whether interrupts
are enabled or not; with interrupts enabled the handler is entered at
the next instruction boundary. RETURN_FROM_IRQ with fewer operands on
the stack than at entry is TRAP_STACK.

Arithmetic (v2) - BINARY_MUL: 33 x 33-bit product, 2 extra clocks;
BINARY_FLOORDIV / BINARY_MOD: Python semantics (the quotient rounds
towards minus infinity, the remainder has the divisor's sign), a radix-2
restoring divider on the magnitudes, 32 extra clocks; a zero divisor is
TRAP_DIV0; a result outside the small-int range is TRAP_OVERFLOW.

Code memory - byte-wide, synchronous read, 1 clock latency (addresses
wrap at 2**CODE_AW, also for operand bytes). Constant pool - VW-bit
words, same timing. Operand stack, locals, globals - flops; locals - one
memory with combinational read (LUT RAM).
Clock - clk only. Reset - synchronous rst_n (active low).
Throughput - multi-cycle FSM, 3 + operand-byte clocks per instruction
(fetch, opcode, operands, execute; LOAD_CONST + 1, BINARY_MUL + 2,
FLOORDIV / MOD + 32), plus the bus handshake for mem32. Matches the
golden model ip/cpu/py_core/model/py_core_model.py instruction for
instruction and clock for clock (tb/python). Version 2.0.0.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - py_core (2026-10-16, updated 2026-10-20)
// Sources:
//   [1] Python Software Foundation, "dis - Disassembler for Python bytecode",
//   https://docs.python.org/3/library/dis.html (CPython stack machine; bytecode is a CPython
//   detail that changes between versions)
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   CPython executes bytecode on a stack machine (LOAD_FAST / STORE_FAST locals, LOAD_CONST,
//   BINARY_OP, COMPARE_OP, jumps, CALL / RETURN_VALUE); the bytecode format is a CPython
//   implementation detail that changes between Python versions.
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches the execution model: operand stack, per-frame locals, globals, constant pool, call
//   / return with a return stack, traps for what the fast path cannot do (heap objects,
//   bigints, RecursionError on too deep calls). Differs: the opcode set is the library's own
//   (py_core_pkg), not CPython bytecode of a given Python version, and ints are 33-bit (CPython
//   ints are unbounded; overflow must trap).
// RESOLVED(REF-PY_CORE-1) [LOW] Opcode set is not CPython bytecode. Resolution: 2026-10-20: the
//   py_core_pkg.sv header maps every py_core opcode to its CPython 3.12 dis counterpart (name,
//   stack effect, argument) and states that pyc.py compiles the Python source's AST directly
//   (not CPython bytecode); tb/python runs pyc.py-compiled programs (programs/prog_v1.py,
//   prog_v2.py) on the RTL against the golden model.
// RESOLVED(REF-PY_CORE-2) [LOW] Small-int overflow. Resolution: 2026-10-20: every arithmetic
//   opcode whose exact result does not fit 33 bits raises TRAP_OVERFLOW (ADD / SUB / LSHIFT by
//   fits_small and the shift-back check, MUL by the 66-bit product's top bits, FLOORDIV for
//   -2**32 // -1; no wrap-around); tests: py_core_tb tests 3 (ADD) and 12 (MUL), and the cocotb
//   random programs (every opcode with the 32-bit corner operands, OVERFLOW ends counted).
```


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys (through sv2v: add the `scripts/sv2v` marker file).
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 1886 LUTs, 1346 flip-flops. Stay within about this budget.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for py_core. Hand-assembles small
programs into a byte-wide code memory and runs them against a
behavioral AXI4-Lite slave with random ready/valid delays. Tests a
while-loop that writes a GPIO register through mem32 (the Python source
is shown next to the bytecode), each trap cause (overflow, type,
illegal opcode, bus error), a full 32-bit register read, and resume
past an emulated instruction, recursive calls, call depth overflow
and RETURN without a caller, the v2 arithmetic (BINARY_MUL, floor
division and modulo with a negative operand, the zero-divisor and
product-overflow traps). Interrupts and WAIT_IRQ are covered by py_soc_tb
and the cocotb comparison with the golden model (tb/python). Prints TEST PASSED on success.
The test tasks are in tests/py_core_tests.sv (`included).
```

There is also a Python (cocotb) test in `tb/python/`; provide an equivalent.

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh py_core --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `py_core_tb` | `py_core_tb` | one test: Self-checking testbench for py_core. |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C cpu/py_core test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
